english: Consider the family of all circles that pass through the origin and have their centres on the line $y=x$. Let $S$ be the orthogonal trajectory of this family that passes through the point $(1,3)$. The curve $S$ is part of a circle which meets the $x$-axis at the origin and at one more point $(\beta,0)$. Then the value of $\beta$ is ______.
hindi: उन सभी वृत्तों के कुल पर विचार कीजिए जो मूलबिन्दु से होकर जाते हैं तथा जिनके केन्द्र रेखा $y=x$ पर हैं। माना कि $S$ इस कुल का बिन्दु $(1,3)$ से होकर जाने वाला लंबकोणीय संछेदी है। वक्र $S$ एक वृत्त का भाग है जो $x$-अक्ष से मूलबिन्दु पर तथा एक अन्य बिन्दु $(\beta,0)$ पर मिलता है। तब $\beta$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Trajectories: $p\to-\dfrac1p$: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac{x^{2}-2xy-y^{2}}{x^{2}+2xy-y^{2}}$, satisfied by the circles $x^{2}+y^{2}=2k(x-y)$ (centres on $y=-x$)
solution_full: A circle through the origin with centre $(c,c)$ is $x^{2}+y^{2}=2c(x+y)$. Differentiate: $2x+2yp=2c(1+p)$, where $p=\dfrac{dy}{dx}$, so $c=\dfrac{x+yp}{1+p}$.

Eliminate $c$: $(x^{2}+y^{2})(1+p)=2(x+y)(x+yp)$. Solving for $p$: $p\left(x^{2}+y^{2}-2xy-2y^{2}\right)=2x^{2}+2xy-x^{2}-y^{2}$, so $p=\dfrac{x^{2}+2xy-y^{2}}{x^{2}-2xy-y^{2}}$ is the slope of the family; this is its differential equation.
For the orthogonal trajectories replace $p$ by $-\dfrac1p$: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=-\dfrac{x^{2}-2xy-y^{2}}{x^{2}+2xy-y^{2}}$.

This equation is homogeneous; by the same elimination it is the differential equation of the circles $x^{2}+y^{2}=2k(x-y)$ (centres $(k,-k)$ on $y=-x$): differentiating gives $k=\dfrac{x+yp}{1-p}$ and eliminating $k$ gives $(x^{2}+y^{2})(1-p)=2(x-y)(x+yp)$, which rearranges to the equation above.
Through $(1,3)$: $1+9=2k(1-3)$, so $k=-\dfrac52$ and the circle is $x^{2}+y^{2}+5x-5y=0$.

Check of orthogonality at $(1,3)$: the family member through $(1,3)$ has $c=\dfrac{10}{8}$, centre $\left(\frac54,\frac54\right)$; the trajectory has centre $\left(-\frac52,\frac52\right)$. The radii to $(1,3)$ are $\left(-\frac14,\frac74\right)$ and $\left(\frac72,\frac12\right)$, with dot product $-\frac78+\frac78=0$, so the circles cut at right angles.
originality_note: New: the orthogonal trajectories of circles through the origin with centres on y = x are circles through the origin with centres on y = -x, read off one member's second x-intercept. Closest known: orthogonal trajectories of x^2 + y^2 = 2cx (circles on the y-axis). Different because: the centre line is oblique, so both the formation and the trajectory equation are less symmetric.
blueprint_concepts: Formation of a differential equation by eliminating arbitrary constants

concept_use.Orthogonal trajectories: The trajectories satisfy the family's slope equation with p replaced by -1/p; they are the circles x^2 + y^2 = 2k(x - y), and the one through (1,3) is selected.
concept_use.Formation of a differential equation by: The family's equation is formed by eliminating c from x^2 + y^2 = 2c(x + y) and its derivative.

key_step: Form the slope equation by eliminating c, replace p by -1/p, recognise the circles with centres on y = -x.
justification: Formation plus the standard orthogonal-trajectory step and a recognition; routine but several steps. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q3 (L2).
